management_notes: Churchill Resources has assembled a management team with credible critical-minerals and junior-mining backgrounds, well-positioned to advance the Grey River Antimony Project. Insider ownership and continued participation in private placements suggest alignment with shareholders. The team has successfully executed on exploration programs in a remote Newfoundland setting and has navigated the capital-markets environment for a pre-resource antimony junior. No red flags on governance or related-party dealings in publicly available filings. Deducting one point given the company remains pre-resource and management execution risk on timeline to a maiden NI 43-101 estimate is unproven.
geology_notes: Grey River is one of the largest known antimony occurrences in North America, underpinned by historical production and high-grade intercepts (reported high-grade zones historically exceeding 5% Sb). The most recent NI 43-101 technical report on file is dated August 2023 (per extracted filings cache); no formal Measured, Indicated, or Inferred resource estimate has been published as of that report. Geology is genuinely promising — antimony mineralisation is well-documented and the structural controls are understood — but the absence of a compliant resource estimate limits the geology score. Score reflects early-exploration/advanced-prospect status: geology thesis is sound but unquantified. An upgrade to 4 is likely on maiden resource publication.
capital_notes: Per April 2026 MD&A (extracted 2026-05-14): 316,681,940 shares issued and outstanding; 342,756,940 fully diluted. Dilution overhead is approximately 26M shares across 2,625,000 warrants and 23,450,000 options — modest relative to the outstanding count (roughly 8.2% dilution to fully diluted). No flow-through tranches were detected in the extraction, meaning there is no near-term FT hold-release overhang suppressing the stock. Share count of ~317M is on the heavier side for a TSXV pre-resource junior but is not structurally problematic given the strategic commodity tailwind. Continued equity raises are expected ahead of a resource estimate; dilution risk is real but manageable. Strike prices and expiry dates for warrants/options were not extractable from the MD&A summary table.
catalyst_notes: The macro catalyst is exceptional: China's 2023 antimony export controls and subsequent tightening in 2024-2025 have driven antimony prices sharply higher and placed North American domestic supply in acute focus from both government and industry. Grey River is one of very few credible near-term antimony development assets in Canada. Near-term company-specific catalysts include: (1) maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate — the highest-value single event for the stock; (2) potential strategic partnership or off-take agreement with a defense/tech/battery materials company; (3) federal or provincial critical minerals funding (Canada's Critical Minerals Strategy and related programs are directly applicable); (4) continued drill results that advance resource confidence. Score 4 rather than 5 because timeline to any of these catalysts remains uncertain and no specific milestones were publicly announced in recently accessible filings.
acquisition_notes: Without a published NI 43-101 resource estimate, a formal P/NAV calculation is not possible. The strategic scarcity value of a significant North American antimony deposit gives CRI real M&A optionality — acquirers include downstream processors, battery/defense supply chain players, and larger mining companies seeking critical minerals exposure. Comparable transaction data for North American antimony assets is thin (antimony M&A is rare in Canada/US). A reasonable thesis exists that the asset would attract a premium to exploration-stage peers in a strategic context, but with no resource to anchor valuation, the acquisition score cannot exceed midpoint. Score would upgrade materially on a maiden resource that allows NAV modelling.
analyst_summary: Churchill Resources (CRI.V) holds the Grey River Antimony Project, one of North America's largest known antimony occurrences, in a period of unprecedented strategic demand for the commodity — China's export restrictions have made domestic Western antimony supply a priority for governments and defense/tech supply chains alike. The investment case is directionally compelling but structurally incomplete: no NI 43-101 resource estimate has been published, leaving the project unquantified and precluding a BUY verdict under the Verdict Framework. The share structure is clean (316.7M issued, 342.8M diluted, no flow-through overhang) and management has maintained the project through exploration without egregious dilution. The primary catalyst to watch is a maiden resource estimate — that single event would likely reprice the stock and could trigger an upgrade to BUY. Monitoring is warranted given the macro tailwinds. Cap-table data sourced from extracted April 2026 MD&A filing; no newer extraction is available. Resource fields are empty as no compliant NI 43-101 estimate has been published.
